h1: The 6 Best Stainless Steel Air Fryers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Stainless Steel Air Fryers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 stainless steel air fryers and air fryer ovens compared on capacity, cooking modes, basket design and counter footprint.
summary: The Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro is the best stainless steel air fryer: 13 functions and super convection in a brushed stainless body. The Cuisinart 6-Quart is the best basket model, and the Cuisinart Toaster Oven is the hybrid for toasting and baking. The Ninja Flip saves counter space, the 4-Quart glass basket avoids coatings, and the Emeril Lagasse handles big batches.
intro: Stainless steel on an air fryer is a styling decision more than a cooking feature. It resists stains, wipes clean and matches the rest of a metal kitchen. What decides how well you cook is the format: a basket that feeds a few servings, or a toaster-oven box that also bakes, broils and holds a whole roast.

The six models here split across both formats. We compared capacity, cooking modes, basket materials and counter footprint, then ranked each on how well it justifies the space it takes. One quiet detail catches shoppers out: on most of these machines, the stainless is the outer shell, and the surface that touches your food is something else entirely, so check the basket material before you pay for the finish.

products.name: Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro
products.verdict: Brushed stainless, 13 cooking functions and super convection for faster cooking.
products.description:
Breville's Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro packs 13 cooking functions covering roasting, air frying and dehydrating into a brushed stainless body. Its super convection system, according to Breville, cuts cooking time by up to 30 percent. A stronger fan moves hot air faster across the food, which is why oven-style air fryers crisp more evenly than weak basket units.

It leads because it replaces a toaster oven, an air fryer and a dehydrator in one footprint, which no basket model can do. The Cuisinart 6-Quart does less but costs far less, in the $50 to $100 bucket against Breville's $200 to $500.

Buy it as the one stainless appliance for everything. The caveat is size and price: it has the largest counter footprint here, and it is overkill if you only air fry frozen snacks.
products.skipIf: You only air fry frozen snacks.

products.name: Cuisinart 6-Quart Air Fryer
products.verdict: A stainless 6-quart basket, five presets and 1800W that holds a 4-lb chicken.
products.description:
Cuisinart's 6-Quart is a basket fryer with a stainless housing, bake, broil, air fry and keep warm modes, and five air-fry presets. The 1800W output holds a 4-lb chicken, which tells you the basket is deep enough for a whole bird. Six quarts is the sweet spot where a small family gets dinner in one batch.

It ranks below the Breville because it cooks in a basket only and has far fewer functions. It beats the 4-quart Cuisinart on capacity, since six quarts feeds a family rather than a couple.

Buy it for simple air frying with minimal fuss. The caveat is that it cannot dehydrate, and it takes more room than a 4-quart. Skip it if you want an appliance to replace the toaster oven.
products.idealFor: Families who want simple air frying.

products.name: Cuisinart Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.verdict: Eight modes, 1800W and an interior that takes up to six slices of toast.
products.description:
The Cuisinart Air Fryer Toaster Oven is a box with eight cooking modes, including air fry, convection, broil and warm, driven by 1800W. The interior takes up to six slices of bread, which is the benchmark for a real toaster oven instead of a gimmick. It replaces two appliances on a counter.

It ranks third because the Breville offers 13 functions and a faster convection system. It wins against the basket fryers for flexibility, since it toasts, bakes and broils too, in the $100 to $200 bucket.

Pick it if you want toast, baking and air frying in one place. The caveat is that it is bigger than a basket unit and preheats more slowly. Skip it if counter space is tight.
cons: Takes longer to preheat than a basket
products.idealFor: Toasting, baking and air frying in one box.

products.name: Ninja Flip Toaster Oven & Air Fryer
products.verdict: Flips up and away to save about half the counter space, with eight cooking functions.
products.description:
The Ninja Flip folds up against the wall when you are done, which Ninja says saves roughly half the counter space. It has eight cooking functions and a stainless steel finish. Flipping removes the penalty that oven-style air fryers usually carry in a small kitchen.

That design is why it ranks fourth: no other model here solves the counter problem. It trades some capacity and function count against the Cuisinart oven and the Breville, so it suits smaller households. It sits in the same $100 to $200 bucket as the Cuisinart oven.

Pick it for a small kitchen or apartment. The caveat is clearance. It needs wall space to flip, and the smaller interior is a poor match for families of four or more.
pros: Saves about half the counter space
products.skipIf: You cook for four or more.

products.name: Cuisinart 4-Quart Glass Basket Air Fryer
products.verdict: Stainless exterior, a PFAS-free borosilicate glass basket and a ClearView window.
products.description:
The Cuisinart 4-Quart pairs a stainless exterior with a PFAS-free borosilicate glass basket and a ClearView window. Glass is chemically inert, so there is no non-stick coating to flake, and the window lets you watch food brown without opening the drawer and dumping heat. It offers five functions.

It ranks fifth because four quarts is small for a family, and the function list is the shortest here. Against the 6-quart Cuisinart, it gives up capacity and presets for a coating-free cooking surface, at a higher $100 to $200 price.

Buy it for one or two people who avoid coatings. The caveat is handling: glass needs more careful treatment than a metal basket. Skip it if you cook for a crowd.
products.idealFor: One or two people avoiding coatings.

products.name: Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door Air Fryer Toaster Oven
products.verdict: A 26-quart French door oven that fits a full roast in one go.
products.description:
The Emeril Lagasse oven has a 26-quart interior with French doors, combining air fryer and multi-cooker functions. French doors open wide with one pull, so you can load a full roast without wrestling a single heavy door. The size fits a roast that a basket air fryer cannot.

It ranks last because it takes the most counter space and is heavy to move, and a large box heats slowly for small jobs. Against the Breville, it offers capacity rather than precision, though its $100 to $200 price is lower.

Buy it for a large family or a host who cooks big. The caveat is footprint: skip it if counter space is limited or if you mostly cook small side dishes.

whatMatters.detail: A basket fryer cooks fast and is easy to clean, but holds a few servings. An oven-style model is larger and can toast, bake and broil. Choose a basket for snacks and sides, an oven for whole meals. Check the listing for words like toaster oven or basket, and weigh the footprint before ordering one.

whatMatters.factor: Stainless is the shell, not the cooking surface
whatMatters.detail: On most air fryers the stainless steel is the outer housing, while the basket or tray inside is coated or glass. If you want to avoid non-stick coatings, look at the basket material, as with the Cuisinart 4-Quart's borosilicate glass, not the exterior. The shell tells you nothing about what touches your food. Marketing photos rarely show the interior.

Four quarts suits one or two people, six quarts feeds a small family, and oven-style models run 20 quarts and above, like the 26QT Emeril Lagasse. Check the cubic feet or quarts on the listing, since a basket can fit less than the number suggests once you account for crowding and air flow around the food.

1800W is the common top figure for countertop units on a standard 15-amp outlet, and higher wattage heats faster. Both the Cuisinart 6-Quart and Cuisinart Toaster Oven list 1800W. Avoid running another high-draw appliance on the same circuit at the same time, because a tripped breaker is the usual result.

Air fryers vent heat from the back or top. Leave a few inches around the unit and do not push it against a wall or under low cabinets. The Ninja Flip needs extra headroom to fold up. Check the manual for clearance figures before choosing a spot, since cramped venting also lengthens cook times. Cramped venting also slows cooking.

faq.q: Is a stainless steel air fryer healthier?
faq.a: Not by itself. Stainless is usually just the outer housing. What matters for coatings is the basket or tray, like the borosilicate glass basket on the Cuisinart 4-Quart, which has no non-stick layer at all.

faq.q: What is the difference between an air fryer and an air fryer oven?
faq.a: A basket air fryer cooks in a drawer. An air fryer oven is a box with racks that can also bake, broil and toast, like the Breville and the Cuisinart Toaster Oven, and it takes more counter space.

faq.q: How big an air fryer do I need?
faq.a: Four quarts suits one or two people, six quarts like the Cuisinart 6-Quart suits a small family, and oven-style units like the Emeril Lagasse suit larger meals. Check the listing for usable capacity, not just the headline number.

faq.q: Can an air fryer oven replace my toaster oven?
faq.a: Yes. The Cuisinart Toaster Oven and Breville Pro both toast, bake and broil. The Cuisinart fits up to six slices of bread, and the Ninja Flip folds away to save counter space between meals.

Basket fryers like the Cuisinart 6-Quart heat quickly, so a short preheat is enough. Oven-style models such as the Breville benefit from a longer preheat. Follow the maker's guidance on the presets for each recipe.

faq.q: How do I clean a stainless air fryer?
faq.a: Wipe the exterior with a soft cloth and mild soap. Wash baskets or trays by hand, or in the dishwasher if the listing says they are dishwasher-safe, and avoid abrasive pads on the glass basket.

finalTake: For most kitchens, the Breville Smart Oven Air Fryer Pro is the right stainless steel air fryer if you want one appliance for everything. Choose the Cuisinart 6-Quart for simple basket cooking, the Cuisinart Toaster Oven for a hybrid, and the Ninja Flip for tight counters. Remember that the stainless is usually the shell, so check the basket material.
